home-energy-audit.title: Home energy audits in Calgary: EnerGuide evaluations, costs and rebates
home-energy-audit.description: Book an EnerGuide home energy audit in Calgary: 26 licensed organizations, local prices, Alberta rebates and what 47% pre-1991 housing means for your upgrade list.
home-energy-audit.lede: 26 NRCan-licensed service organizations deliver EnerGuide home evaluations in Calgary. Here's what one costs, what it tends to find in Calgary houses, and which Alberta rebates it unlocks.

sections.h2: What an evaluation finds in Calgary homes
sections.html:
Of Calgary's 379,710 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 10% were built before 1961 and 47% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census. The typical Calgary house dates from 1991–1995, and an evaluation is how you find out what that means for yours: the blower door measures air leakage, the advisor inspects the attic, walls, basement, windows and heating system, and the report ranks upgrades by what they'd save.

Calgary gets about 4,876 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −26.2°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Calgary International. That's about 24% more heating demand than the middle of the 70 cities we cover. The more heating a climate needs, the more each fix is worth, which is why the evaluation's ranked list matters more in some cities than others.

In the Calgary area, 74% of households heat mainly with a forced-air furnace and 8% with a boiler and radiators; natural gas is the main heating energy for 73% of households and electricity for 13% (Statistics Canada, 2023). The heating system on the report shapes the recommendations: a forced-air furnace invites a ducted heat pump, electric baseboards a ductless one.

There's no provincial rebate or price list; the City of Edmonton's guidance is to expect more than $400 and to get two or three quotes.

Most providers quote the initial (pre-upgrade) and follow-up (post-upgrade) visits separately. Rebate programs that pay on measured improvement need both, so ask for the combined price.

• Initial evaluation, about 2–3 hours. The advisor measures and inspects the house and runs the blower door test.
  • Report and EnerGuide rating. You get the home's energy rating in gigajoules per year and a list of recommended upgrades with estimated savings.
  • Do the work. Most rebate programs only count upgrades done after the initial evaluation.
  • Follow-up evaluation. A second visit measures the improvement, which is what most rebates pay on.

blower-door-test.description: Where to get a blower door test in Calgary, what it costs, and why air leakage matters with 4,876 heating degree-days a year and 10% of houses built before 1961.
blower-door-test.lede: A blower door test measures how leaky a house is and shows where the leaks are. In Calgary, with about 4,876 heating degree-days a year, every leak runs up the heating bill for most of the year.

sections.h2: Why air leakage matters in Calgary
sections.html:
Calgary gets about 4,876 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −26.2°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Calgary International. That's about 24% more heating demand than the middle of the 70 cities we cover.

Of Calgary's 379,710 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 10% were built before 1961 and 47% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census. Older houses usually test leakier than newer ones, and an EnerGuide report compares your result with homes of the same era, so you can see whether your house is typical or a problem.

• Combustion safety. In the Calgary area, the main heating energy is natural gas for 73% of households. A tighter house changes how fuel-burning appliances vent, so the spillage check should be repeated after serious air sealing. Combustion safety testing in Calgary
  • Radon. Sealing shifts the pressure balance between the house and the soil. Health Canada's 2012 survey found 8.1% of 86 homes tested in the Calgary Health Region health region above the guideline. The larger 2024 Cross-Canada survey reports 15.5% (1 in 6) of houses at or above the guideline for Calgary Metro Area (Calgary CMA). Test before and after big air-sealing jobs. Radon testing in Calgary

A blower door test is part of every EnerGuide evaluation rather than a separate purchase. There's no provincial rebate or price list; the City of Edmonton's guidance is to expect more than $400 and to get two or three quotes.

• A calibrated fan is fitted into an exterior door and pulls air out until the house is at 50 pascals, the standard test pressure.
  • The result is air changes per hour at 50 Pa (ACH50): how many times an hour the whole volume of air would leak out and be replaced at that pressure.
  • While the fan runs, you and the advisor walk the house and feel for leaks at the attic hatch, rim joists, pot lights, trim and plumbing and wiring penetrations.
  • A second test after the work shows what changed, and it is what most rebates pay on.

The blower door test in detail.

sections.h2: What the camera finds in Calgary houses

heat-loss-calculation.title: Heat loss calculation in Calgary: sizing a heat pump for −26.2°C
heat-loss-calculation.description: A CSA F280 room-by-room heat loss calculation for Calgary homes, sized to the local −26.2°C design temperature: why it matters for heat pumps, what it costs and who does it.
heat-loss-calculation.lede: The heat loss calculation is how a heat pump or furnace gets sized for your house, and the key input is the design temperature: −26.2°C for Calgary, from NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Calgary International.

sections.h2: Why the design temperature matters in Calgary
sections.html:
−26.2°C is the 12th-coldest design temperature of the 70 cities we cover. The F280 calculation works out how much heat each room loses on that design day, from the house's actual walls, windows, air leakage and ceiling insulation.

At −26.2°C, a cold-climate heat pump sized to the calculation can carry most of the season, and the number shows how much backup heat the coldest days need.

In the Calgary area, 74% of households heat mainly with a forced-air furnace and 8% with a boiler and radiators; natural gas is the main heating energy for 73% of households and electricity for 13% (Statistics Canada, 2023).

Contractors who size by square footage routinely oversize. An oversized heat pump costs more to buy, cycles on and off, dehumidifies poorly in summer and wears faster. An undersized one leans on backup heat. The F280 report is the evidence either way, and it's worth having before you compare quotes.

About $150–$400 as a standalone calculation (a September 2026 planning range; quotes vary). Many energy advisors bundle it with an EnerGuide evaluation, which also gives the calculation measured air-leakage data instead of an assumption.

providers.heading: NRCan-licensed service organizations serving Calgary
providers.note: Many energy advisors also do room-by-room CSA F280 calculations for an extra fee; HVAC designers do them too. Ask for the F280 report itself, not just an equipment recommendation.

ventilation-assessment.h1: Ventilation and humidity assessments in Calgary
ventilation-assessment.title: Ventilation and humidity assessment in Calgary: condensation, mold and HRVs
ventilation-assessment.description: Why Calgary homes get window condensation and musty air, what a ventilation and humidity assessment measures, and when an HRV or ERV makes sense. 36% of local houses were built since 2001.
ventilation-assessment.lede: Condensation on windows, musty basements and stuffy bedrooms are ventilation and humidity problems, and they're easy to confuse with insulation problems. A ventilation assessment measures which one you have.

sections.h2: Why Calgary homes get humidity problems
sections.html:
Calgary gets about 4,876 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −26.2°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Calgary International. On Calgary's coldest days, window glass and poorly insulated corners get cold enough for condensation at humidity levels that feel normal indoors, so winter humidity needs to stay at the lower end of the comfortable range.

Of Calgary's 379,710 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 10% were built before 1961 and 47% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census. Newer houses (36% of Calgary's were built since 2001) are tight and usually have an HRV or ERV that needs balancing and cleaning. Older houses that get air-sealed can lose the accidental ventilation they used to rely on.

• Relative humidity in living areas and the basement.
  • Actual airflow from bath and kitchen fans, and whether they vent outside rather than into the attic.
  • How much fresh air the house gets, and whether an HRV or ERV is balanced.

The ventilation and humidity assessment in detail.
Mold and air quality testing in Calgary · Radon testing in Calgary

faq.q: HRV or ERV?
faq.a: Both bring in fresh air and recover heat. An ERV also transfers some moisture, which helps keep very dry winter air from getting drier; an HRV suits houses that tend to run humid.

faq.q: Why did condensation appear after we got new windows?
faq.a: Tighter windows cut accidental air leakage, so humidity builds up. The fix is usually controlled ventilation, not leakier windows.

faq.q: Is a ventilation assessment part of an EnerGuide evaluation in Calgary?
faq.a: Advisors assess ventilation and humidity during the evaluation; HRV or ERV sizing may be an extra service.

sections.h2: What inspections find in Calgary attics
sections.html:
Of Calgary's 379,710 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 10% were built before 1961 and 47% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census. Attics in older houses commonly have a fraction of today's recommended insulation, and top-ups done over the years often buried air leaks instead of sealing them first.

Calgary gets about 4,876 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −26.2°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Calgary International. That's about 24% more heating demand than the middle of the 70 cities we cover. The colder the climate, the faster added attic insulation pays for itself.

Vermiculite. Loose, pebbly, grey-brown or silver-gold insulation may contain asbestos. Health Canada's advice is not to disturb it; have it sampled before any attic work. Asbestos and vermiculite testing in Calgary

sections.h2: The right order for the work
sections.html:
• Seal the air leaks first: top plates, pot lights, plumbing stacks, the hatch.
  • Fix ventilation baffles so new insulation doesn't block soffit vents.
  • Then top up the insulation. Burying unsealed leaks under new insulation wastes much of the benefit.

What an attic inspection checks.

Alberta is a retail market: the distributor owns the wires and pipes, but you may buy the energy itself from a retailer. Your usage history sits with whoever bills you.

  • ENMAX Power: ENMAX Power (the wires company) doesn't bill homes, so usage history comes from your retailer's bills or online account, e.g. ENMAX Energy MyAccount for ENMAX retail and Rate of Last Resort customers. No distributor usage portal or Green Button found; the ENMAX MyAccount page only confirms bills and payments. Link

Calgary gets about 4,876 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −26.2°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Calgary International. Weather-normalizing your bills against those degree-days separates heating from baseload (lights, appliances, hot water), so you can see how much of the bill a heating upgrade can actually touch, and compare a mild year with a harsh one fairly.

radon-testing.title: Radon testing in Calgary: local levels, test kits and certified professionals
radon-testing.description: Radon in Calgary: Health Canada survey results for the Calgary Health Region region (8.1% above the guideline), how to test for 3+ months, where to get kits and C-NRPP professionals locally.
radon-testing.lede: Radon is invisible, has no smell, and is the second-leading cause of lung cancer in Canada. In Health Canada's national survey, 8.1% of homes tested in the Calgary Health Region health region were above the guideline, and the only way to know about your house is to test it.

sections.html:
Health Canada's 2012 survey found 8.1% of 86 homes tested in the Calgary Health Region health region above the guideline. The larger 2024 Cross-Canada survey reports 15.5% (1 in 6) of houses at or above the guideline for Calgary Metro Area (Calgary CMA).

The two surveys aren't directly comparable: the 2024 study pooled about 69,000 volunteer tests and more of them were taken in basements, which partly explains its higher numbers. Neither can tell you about a single house, because neighbouring homes can differ widely.

• Use a long-term test of at least three months, with most of it in the heating season, which gives the most conservative result.
  • Place the detector in the lowest level you spend four or more hours a day in, away from drafts, and follow the kit's instructions.
  • If the result is above 200 Bq/m³, Health Canada recommends fixing it within a year, sooner if it's much higher.

Our full radon testing guide.

• Alberta Lung supports free radon-monitor lending at libraries including Edmonton Public Library and Red Deer Public Library; long-term kits are sold separately.
  • For a professional measurement or mitigation, search the C-NRPP directory by your Calgary postal code; it lists certified measurement and mitigation professionals.

• Alberta's building code requires a soil-gas barrier and a radon rough-in in new homes.
  • The Canadian Lung Association's Lungs Matter program offers up to $1,500 toward mitigation for households with low to moderate incomes or a lung cancer diagnosis.
  • If your level is high, mitigation (usually a sub-slab depressurization fan system installed by a C-NRPP-certified professional) typically costs $2,000–$4,000.

faq.q: Is radon a problem in Calgary?
faq.a: Health Canada's 2012 survey found 8.1% of 86 homes tested in the Calgary Health Region health region above the guideline. The larger 2024 Cross-Canada survey reports 15.5% (1 in 6) of houses at or above the guideline for Calgary Metro Area (Calgary CMA). Any home can have high radon, so Health Canada recommends testing every home.

faq.q: How long should a radon test take?
faq.a: At least three months, with most of it during the heating season. Short tests can't tell you your long-term average.

faq.q: Where can I get a radon test kit in Calgary?
faq.a: Alberta Lung supports free radon-monitor lending at libraries including Edmonton Public Library and Red Deer Public Library; long-term kits are sold separately. Hardware stores and lung associations also sell long-term kits for about $30–$60.

faq.q: What does radon mitigation cost?
faq.a: Typically $2,000–$4,000 for a sub-slab depressurization system installed by a C-NRPP-certified professional.

carbon-monoxide-testing.title: Carbon monoxide testing in Calgary: the Alberta alarm rules and appliance checks
carbon-monoxide-testing.description: CO safety for Calgary homes: what Alberta law requires, why it matters with 73% of households heating with natural gas, where alarms go and how appliances get checked.
carbon-monoxide-testing.lede: Carbon monoxide is odourless and can kill. Alberta requires CO alarms in new homes with a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage; for existing homes the province calls them highly recommended rather than mandatory.

sections.html: Alberta requires CO alarms in new homes with a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage; for existing homes the province calls them highly recommended rather than mandatory.

In the Calgary area, the main heating energy is natural gas for 73% of households (Statistics Canada, 2023). Any fuel-burning appliance, fireplace or attached garage is a potential CO source.

Single-detached houses make up 55% of Calgary's households; many have an attached garage, another reason to put an alarm near the door into the house.

• Alarms next to sleeping areas and on every storey, tested monthly and replaced by their end-of-life date (usually 7 to 10 years).
  • Annual service of fuel-burning appliances by a licensed technician.
  • A combustion spillage test during an energy evaluation, which catches a venting problem before it produces CO.

Our carbon monoxide guide · Combustion safety testing in Calgary

faq.q: Are carbon monoxide alarms mandatory in Calgary?
faq.a: Alberta requires CO alarms in new homes with a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage; for existing homes the province calls them highly recommended rather than mandatory.

faq.q: Where should CO alarms go?
faq.a: Outside every sleeping area and on every storey, following the manufacturer's instructions. Some rules also call for one near a fuel-burning appliance or the door from an attached garage.

faq.q: How long do CO alarms last?
faq.a: Most have an end-of-life date of 7 to 10 years printed on the unit; replace them by then even if they still beep when tested.

mold-testing.h1: Mold and air quality testing in Calgary
mold-testing.title: Mold testing in Calgary: air quality sampling and finding the moisture source
mold-testing.description: Mold and indoor air quality testing in Calgary: when sampling is worth $300–$600, why cold winters cause condensation, and how to find an accredited lab.
mold-testing.lede: Mold sampling tells you whether there's a hidden mold problem and roughly where. It doesn't tell you why, and fixing the moisture source is the actual cure.

sections.h2: Why mold shows up in Calgary homes
sections.html:
Calgary gets about 4,876 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −26.2°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Calgary International. On cold days, exterior corners, closets on outside walls and window frames get cold enough for condensation, which is where mold usually starts in Calgary houses.

Of Calgary's 379,710 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 10% were built before 1961 and 47% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census. Older basements without a moisture barrier and houses that were air-sealed without adding ventilation are common trouble spots.

• You smell mustiness but can't find the source.
  • After a leak or flood, to check that cleanup worked.
  • Before buying an older house with signs of past water damage.

If you can see mould, you usually don't need a test to know it's there; you need to fix the moisture and clean it up properly.

No Canadian province has a mandatory mould standard for homes. Health Canada's guideline sets no numerical limit: it says to fix moisture problems and clean up visible mould.

Ask any Calgary tester which lab analyzes their samples, and look for one accredited under AIHA's EMLAP program for environmental microbiology. Pair sampling with a ventilation and humidity assessment, which finds the cause.

Ventilation and humidity assessments in Calgary · Our mold and indoor air quality guide

faq.q: How much does mold testing cost in Calgary?
faq.a: Plan on about $300–$600 for a typical sampling visit (a September 2026 planning range); lab fees for extra samples add to that.

faq.q: Do I need a test if I can see mould?
faq.a: Usually not. Visible mould needs cleanup and a fix for the moisture source. Testing helps most when you suspect mould you can't see.

faq.q: Is there a legal mould limit for homes in Canada?
faq.a: No. Health Canada sets no numerical limit; its guidance is to control moisture and clean up mould. Quebec has a voluntary handling standard.

asbestos-testing.h1: Asbestos and vermiculite testing in Calgary
asbestos-testing.title: Asbestos testing in Calgary: vermiculite, labs and the Alberta rules
asbestos-testing.description: Asbestos and vermiculite testing in Calgary, where 47% of houses were built before 1991: what to sample, lab costs and the Alberta rules for renovation.
asbestos-testing.lede: About 180,000 Calgary houses (47%) were built before 1991, when asbestos still turned up in insulation, flooring, plaster and duct wrap. A lab test before renovation is the only way to know.

sections.h2: Where asbestos shows up in Calgary houses
sections.html:
Of Calgary's 379,710 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 10% were built before 1961 and 47% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census.

  • Vermiculite attic insulation: loose, pebbly, grey-brown or silver-gold granules.
  • Vinyl floor tiles and their adhesive, textured ceilings and some plaster.
  • Duct wrap and pipe insulation on older heating systems.

Alberta's OHS Code requires certified workers for asbestos removal, and anyone planning asbestos removal, or demolition or renovation of a building containing asbestos, must notify Alberta OHS at least 72 hours before starting.

Whatever the rules, don't sand, cut or remove suspect material yourself before it's tested.

A trained assessor takes small samples, and an accredited lab analyzes them; plan on about $50–$150 per sample. Asbestos labs in Canada are typically accredited under NIST's NVLAP program.

Our asbestos and vermiculite guide · Attic inspections in Calgary

faq.q: Do I need an asbestos test before renovating in Calgary?
faq.a: If the house was built before 1991 and the work will disturb insulation, flooring, plaster or duct wrap, test first. Alberta's OHS Code requires certified workers for asbestos removal, and anyone planning asbestos removal, or demolition or renovation of a building containing asbestos, must notify Alberta OHS at least 72 hours before starting.

faq.q: How much does asbestos testing cost?
faq.a: About $50–$150 per lab sample, plus the assessor's visit. Abatement, if needed, is quoted separately.

faq.q: What should I do if I have vermiculite in the attic?
faq.a: Leave it alone, keep the attic closed, and have it sampled before any attic work. Health Canada advises against disturbing it or removing it yourself.

lead-paint-testing.title: Lead paint testing in Calgary: which homes are at risk and how to test
lead-paint-testing.description: 10% of Calgary's houses were built before 1961, when lead paint was common. How to test with $15–$40 swabs or a lab, and how to renovate safely.
lead-paint-testing.lede: Health Canada says a home built before 1960 probably has lead paint somewhere. That's 10% of Calgary's houses (built before 1961, per the 2021 Census), plus exterior paint on many of the 38% built from 1961 to 1990.

sections.h2: Which Calgary homes are at risk
sections.html:
Of Calgary's 379,710 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 10% were built before 1961 and 47% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census.

  • Built before 1960: probably has lead-based paint (Health Canada).
  • Built 1960–1990: exterior paint may contain lead, and interior paint may contain smaller amounts.
  • Built after 1990: consumer paints were virtually lead-free by then.

• Swab kits ($15–$40) give a quick screen of the surfaces you plan to disturb.
  • For certainty, send paint chips to a lab accredited under AIHA's ELLAP program, or hire a firm with an X-ray fluorescence (XRF) analyzer.
  • Test before sanding, stripping or replacing old windows and trim.

Our lead paint guide.

Don't dry-sand, use a heat gun or power-wash it. Contain the work area, mist surfaces, clean with a HEPA vacuum, and keep children and pregnant people away until cleanup is done. No province has a lead-paint rule aimed at homeowners, but contractors in B.C. and Yukon must include lead in pre-renovation or demolition hazard inspections.

faq.q: Does my Calgary house have lead paint?
faq.a: If it was built before 1960, probably; 1960–1990, possibly on the exterior. Test the surfaces you plan to disturb.

faq.q: Are lead test swabs reliable?
faq.a: They are a useful screen. For renovation decisions, confirm with a lab analysis of paint chips or an XRF reading.

faq.q: What does lead paint testing cost?
faq.a: Swab kits run about $15–$40; lab analysis and XRF testing cost more and are quoted by the firm.

well-water-testing.title: Well water testing in Calgary: how to test and what it costs in Alberta
well-water-testing.description: Private well water testing in Calgary: most homes are on city water, but some rely on wells. How Alberta's testing program works, what it costs and how often to test.
well-water-testing.lede: Almost all Calgary homes are on the City's municipal water system, so private wells are rare. If yours is, here's how testing works in Alberta.

sections.html: Almost all Calgary homes are on the City's municipal water system, so private wells are rare.

Alberta Health Services tests private well water free, for bacteria plus chemistry and trace metals; pick up bottles at AHS facilities. Test for bacteria twice a year and for chemistry every three years.

• Bacteria (total coliforms and E. coli): at least once a year, and after flooding, heavy rain or work on the well.
  • Nitrate, especially near farmland or septic systems.
  • Metals and naturally occurring contaminants such as arsenic, uranium or manganese when a well is new and every few years after, depending on local geology.

Our well water guide.

faq.q: Is well water testing free in Alberta?
faq.a: Alberta Health Services tests private well water free, for bacteria plus chemistry and trace metals; pick up bottles at AHS facilities. Test for bacteria twice a year and for chemistry every three years.

faq.q: How often should I test my well?
faq.a: For bacteria, at least once a year and after flooding, heavy rain or well work; many health units recommend more often. Test chemistry when the well is new and every few years after.

faq.q: Are private wells common in Calgary?
faq.a: Almost all Calgary homes are on the City's municipal water system, so private wells are rare.

commercial-energy-audit.title: Commercial energy audits in Calgary: reporting rules and incentives
commercial-energy-audit.description: Commercial and multi-unit building energy audits in Calgary: ASHRAE levels, no mandatory reporting rule, and 1 utility or government incentive for audits and studies.
commercial-energy-audit.lede: Offices, apartment buildings, retail and industrial sites get engineering energy audits rather than EnerGuide evaluations. Here's what applies in Calgary: no mandatory reporting rule and 1 incentive program we found for audits and studies.

sections.h2: Reporting rules that apply in Calgary
sections.html: • BenchmarkYYC (voluntary): Voluntary benchmarking program; owners sign up and accept terms. Any building type on Portfolio Manager's list, any size, in Calgary. Participants get an annual scorecard, discounted training and notices of retrofit funding, plus three complimentary virtual decarbonization plans. No mandatory by-law found; an earlier Council committee report (UCS2018-0314) preferred voluntary benchmarking. Source

• Clean Energy Improvement Program (CEIP) - commercial (Alberta Municipalities with participating municipalities): Property-assessed financing (not a grant) of up to 100% of eligible energy-efficiency and renewable upgrade costs, repaid through the property tax bill (terms up to 20 years for some upgrades). Pre-qualification requires an ASHRAE Level 2 audit report, or a quote showing one is booked (plus a feasibility study for non-solar renewables); a post-project memo from an energy-audit engineering consultant is also required. Details

• Level 1, walk-through: a site visit and bill review that benchmarks the building and lists low-cost measures.
  • Level 2, energy survey and analysis: where the energy goes, with savings and cost estimates per measure. Most incentive applications use this level.
  • Level 3, detailed analysis: monitoring and modelling for capital-intensive projects.

Ask which level a quote covers. Audits are done by engineering firms and energy consultants; look for a P.Eng. and credentials such as the Certified Energy Manager (CEM). How commercial energy audits work.

faq.q: Do Calgary buildings have to report energy use?
faq.a: We found no mandatory reporting rule for Calgary buildings as of September 28, 2026.

faq.q: Are there incentives for commercial energy audits in Calgary?
faq.a: Yes: Clean Energy Improvement Program (CEIP) - commercial. Check eligibility and pre-approval rules before you commission the audit.

faq.q: What does a commercial energy audit cost?
faq.a: It depends on the building's size and the ASHRAE level. Get quotes that state the level and the deliverables.
